questions.prompt: Septic shock is frequently caused by infections involving
questions.suggestedLabel: A. gram-negative endotoxin-producing bacteria.
questions.suggestedRationale: Septic shock is commonly triggered by gram-negative bacteria and their endotoxin.

questions.prompt: Excessive fluid in the pericardial space causes
questions.suggestedLabel: C. reduced venous return.
questions.suggestedRationale: Excess pericardial fluid (tamponade) limits filling and therefore reduces venous return and cardiac output.

questions.prompt: Varicose ulcers may develop and be slow to heal because
options: leg muscles are painful, restricting movement.
edema reduces arterial blood supply to the area.
emboli form in damaged veins, leading to local ischemia.
valves in veins restrict blood flow.
questions.suggestedLabel: B. edema reduces arterial blood supply to the area.
questions.suggestedRationale: Edema around varicose veins can impair arterial perfusion of the skin, so ulcers form and heal slowly.

questions.prompt: Prophylactic antibacterial drugs such as amoxicillin are given to patients with certain congenital heart defects or damaged heart valves immediately before invasive procedures to prevent
questions.suggestedLabel: B. infectious endocarditis.
questions.suggestedRationale: Periprocedural antibiotics are given to prevent infective endocarditis in patients with certain valve or congenital lesions.

questions.prompt: In a child with acute rheumatic fever, arrhythmias may develop due to the presence of
questions.suggestedLabel: B. myocarditis.
questions.suggestedRationale: In rheumatic fever, myocarditis is the lesion most likely to cause arrhythmias.

questions.prompt: In a child with ventricular septal defect, altered blood flow
options: leads to increased stroke volume from the left ventricle.
results in unoxygenated blood in the systemic circulation.
questions.suggestedLabel: D. is called a left-to-right shunt
questions.suggestedRationale: A VSD usually shunts blood from the higher-pressure left ventricle to the right ventricle (left-to-right).

questions.prompt: In patients with congestive heart failure, ACE inhibitor drugs are useful because they
questions.suggestedLabel: A. reduce renin and aldosterone secretion.
questions.suggestedRationale: ACE inhibitors reduce angiotensin II and therefore reduce aldosterone (and the effects of renin–angiotensin signaling).

questions.prompt: Which of the following compensations that develop in patients with congestive heart failure eventually increase the workload of the heart?
options: Faster heart rate and cardiomegaly, peripheral vasoconstriction
Faster heart rate and cardiomegaly, peripheral vasoconstriction, increased secretion of renin
questions.suggestedLabel: E. Faster heart rate and cardiomegaly, peripheral vasoconstriction, increased secretion of renin
questions.suggestedRationale: Tachycardia, cardiomegaly, vasoconstriction, and renin–aldosterone activation all eventually increase the work of the failing heart.

questions.prompt: The right side of the heart would fail first in the case of
options: large infarction in the right ventricle.
questions.suggestedRationale: A large right-ventricular infarct or advanced COPD/pulmonary hypertension overloads the right side first; mitral stenosis and essential hypertension strain the left side first.

questions.prompt: A very rapid heart rate reduces cardiac output because
options: conduction through the AV node is impaired.
questions.suggestedLabel: D. ventricular filling is reduced.
questions.suggestedRationale: A very rapid rate shortens diastole, so ventricular filling and stroke volume fall.

questions.prompt: More extensive permanent damage is likely when a myocardial infarction is caused by
questions.suggestedLabel: C. a thrombus.
questions.suggestedRationale: An occlusive thrombus in situ is more likely to cause extensive, permanent infarction than a transient embolus or an arrhythmia alone.

questions.prompt: Heart block, in which a conduction delay at the AV node results in intermittent missed ventricular contractions, is called
questions.suggestedLabel: B. second-degree block.
questions.suggestedRationale: Second-degree AV block produces intermittent dropped ventricular beats.

questions.prompt: Septic shock differs from hypovolemic shock in that it is frequently manifested by
questions.suggestedLabel: A. fever and flushed face.
questions.suggestedRationale: Early (distributive) septic shock often presents with fever and warm, flushed skin, unlike cool, pale hypovolemic shock.

questions.prompt: Confirmation of the diagnosis of a myocardial infarction would include
options: marked leukocytosis and increased erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR).
elevation of cardiac isoenzymes in serum.
questions.suggestedRationale: MI is confirmed by characteristic ECG changes plus elevated cardiac biomarkers; pain pattern and nonspecific inflammation are less definitive.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT true of the drug nitroglycerin?
options: It decreases myocardial workload by causing systemic vasodilation.
It may be administered sublingually, transdermally, or by oral spray.
Dizziness or syncope may follow a sublingual dose.
questions.suggestedLabel: D. It strengthens the myocardial contraction
questions.suggestedRationale: Nitroglycerin is a vasodilator that reduces workload; it does not strengthen contraction.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is considered to be the most dangerous arrhythmia?
questions.suggestedLabel: C. Ventricular fibrillation
questions.suggestedRationale: Ventricular fibrillation produces no effective cardiac output and is the most immediately lethal arrhythmia listed.

questions.prompt: A cardiac pacemaker would most likely be inserted in cases of
questions.suggestedLabel: B. heart block.
questions.suggestedRationale: A pacemaker is used for symptomatic or high-grade heart block; defibrillation (not a pacing indication here) treats ventricular fibrillation.

questions.prompt: A common adverse effect of many antihypertensive medications is
questions.suggestedLabel: A. orthostatic hypotension.
questions.suggestedRationale: Orthostatic hypotension is a common adverse effect of many antihypertensive drugs.

questions.prompt: The classic early manifestation(s) of left-sided congestive heart failure is/are ____, whereas the early indicator(s) of right-sided failure is/are _______.
options: palpitations and periodic chest pain; shortness of breath on exertion
swelling of the ankles and abdomen; chest pain
shortness of breath on exertion or lying down; swelling of the ankles
coughing up frothy sputum; hepatomegaly and splenomegaly
questions.suggestedLabel: C. shortness of breath on exertion or lying down; swelling of the ankles
questions.suggestedRationale: Left-sided failure presents early with dyspnea on exertion or lying down; right-sided failure presents with peripheral edema such as ankle swelling.

questions.prompt: Shock develops in patients with severe burns as a result of
questions.suggestedLabel: B. pain and loss of plasma.
questions.suggestedRationale: Burn shock is driven by pain and massive plasma loss into injured tissues, not primarily by hemorrhage.

questions.prompt: With shock, anaerobic cell metabolism and decreased renal blood flow cause
questions.suggestedLabel: B. metabolic acidosis.
questions.suggestedRationale: Anaerobic metabolism and poor renal perfusion in shock produce metabolic acidosis.

questions.prompt: A prolonged period of shock is likely to cause
options: damage to, and increased permeability of, pulmonary capillaries.
increased permeability of the glomerular capillaries of the kidneys.
increased pH of blood and body fluids.
questions.suggestedLabel: A. damage to, and increased permeability of, pulmonary capillaries.
questions.suggestedRationale: Prolonged shock can injure pulmonary capillaries (shock lung/ARDS) and increase their permeability.

questions.prompt: Neurogenic (vasogenic) shock results from systemic vasodilation due to
options: increased peripheral resistance and less blood in the microcirculation.
increased permeability of all the blood vessels, leading to hypovolemia.
increased capacity of the vascular system and reduced venous return
questions.suggestedLabel: D. increased capacity of the vascular system and reduced venous return
questions.suggestedRationale: Neurogenic shock is loss of vasomotor tone, so vascular capacity rises and venous return falls.

questions.prompt: Why does anaphylactic shock cause severe hypoxia very quickly?
options: Bronchoconstriction and bronchial edema reduce airflow.
Heart rate and contractility are reduced.
questions.suggestedLabel: B. Bronchoconstriction and bronchial edema reduce airflow.
questions.suggestedRationale: Anaphylaxis causes rapid hypoxia from bronchoconstriction and airway edema as well as vasodilation.

questions.prompt: A compensation for shock would include
questions.suggestedLabel: A. increased heart rate and oliguria.
questions.suggestedRationale: Compensated shock includes tachycardia and oliguria (sympathetic and renin–aldosterone effects).

questions.prompt: What are the early signs of circulatory shock?
questions.suggestedRationale: Early signs include pale moist skin and anxiety or restlessness. Loss of consciousness is late; a rapid pulse occurs early, but “strong” is only briefly true, and no option lists 1, 3, and 4 together.

questions.prompt: Shock follows a myocardial infarction when
options: the stress response causes general vasodilation.
fluid is lost into ischemic tissues.
a large portion of the myocardium is damaged.
questions.suggestedLabel: D. a large portion of the myocardium is damaged.
questions.suggestedRationale: Cardiogenic shock after MI occurs when a large portion of the myocardium is damaged and pump function collapses.

questions.prompt: An echocardiogram is used to demonstrate any abnormal
questions.suggestedLabel: B. movement of the heart valves.
questions.suggestedRationale: Echocardiography shows chamber and valve motion (and estimated flows); it is not the test of the conduction system itself.

questions.prompt: The term intermittent claudication refers to
options: sensory deficit in the legs due to damage to nerves.
ischemic muscle pain in the legs, particularly with exercise.
dry, cyanotic skin with superficial ulcers.
questions.suggestedLabel: C. ischemic muscle pain in the legs, particularly with exercise.
questions.suggestedRationale: Intermittent claudication is ischemic leg-muscle pain, typically brought on by exercise and relieved by rest.

questions.prompt: Atherosclerosis in the iliac or femoral arteries is likely to cause which of the following?
options: Strong rapid pulses in the legs
questions.suggestedRationale: Iliac or femoral atherosclerosis can cause claudication and, when severe, ischemic or gangrenous ulcers; pulses are weakened, not strong.

questions.prompt: Uncontrolled hypertension is most likely to cause ischemia and loss of function in the
options: kidneys, brain, and retinas of the eye.
questions.suggestedLabel: A. kidneys, brain, and retinas of the eye.
questions.suggestedRationale: The key target organs of uncontrolled hypertension include the kidneys, brain, and retina.

questions.prompt: Pericarditis may be caused by
questions.suggestedRationale: Pericarditis can follow infection, immune reactions, injury, or malignancy — all of the listed causes.

questions.prompt: Pericarditis causes a reduction in cardiac output as a result of which of the following?
options: Delays in the conduction system, interfering with cardiac rhythm
Weak myocardial contractions due to friction rub
Excess fluid in the pericardial cavity, which decreases ventricular filling
Incompetent valves, which allow regurgitation of blood
questions.suggestedLabel: C. Excess fluid in the pericardial cavity, which decreases ventricular filling
questions.suggestedRationale: Pericardial effusion limits diastolic filling, so stroke volume and cardiac output fall.

questions.prompt: Septic emboli, a common complication of infective endocarditis, are a result of the fact that
options: vegetations are loosely attached and fragile.
the valves are no longer competent.
questions.suggestedLabel: A. vegetations are loosely attached and fragile.
questions.suggestedRationale: Infective vegetations are fragile and can break off as septic emboli.

questions.prompt: The initial effect on the heart in cases of rheumatic fever is
options: infection in the heart by hemolytic streptococci.
highly virulent microbes causing vegetations on the heart valves.
acute inflammation in all layers of the heart due to abnormal immune response.
questions.suggestedLabel: D. acute inflammation in all layers of the heart due to abnormal immune response.
questions.suggestedRationale: The initial cardiac injury in rheumatic fever is a pancarditis from an abnormal immune response, not direct streptococcal infection of the heart.

questions.prompt: Cyanosis occurs in children with tetralogy of Fallot because
options: more carbon dioxide is present in the circulating blood.
a large amount of hemoglobin in the general circulation is unoxygenated.
the pulmonary circulation is overloaded and congested.
the circulation is sluggish (slow) throughout the system.
questions.suggestedLabel: B. a large amount of hemoglobin in the general circulation is unoxygenated.
questions.suggestedRationale: Cyanosis appears when a large amount of unoxygenated hemoglobin reaches the systemic circulation.

questions.prompt: Unoxygenated blood enters the systemic circulation in children with tetralogy of Fallot because
options: the aorta and pulmonary artery have exchanged positions.
pulmonary stenosis changes the ventricular pressures.
the left ventricular wall has hypertrophied.
the septal defect allows exchange of blood between the atria.
questions.suggestedLabel: B. pulmonary stenosis changes the ventricular pressures.
questions.suggestedRationale: Pulmonary stenosis raises right-ventricular pressure, so blood shunts right-to-left through the VSD into the overriding aorta.

questions.prompt: Which of the following describes the blood flow occurring with a ventricular septal defect?
options: From the left ventricle to the right ventricle
From the right ventricle to the left ventricle
Increased cardiac output from the left ventricle
Mixed oxygenated and unoxygenated blood in the systemic circulation
questions.suggestedLabel: A. From the left ventricle to the right ventricle
questions.suggestedRationale: In a typical VSD, blood flows from the higher-pressure left ventricle into the right ventricle.

questions.prompt: A sign of aortic stenosis is
options: congestion in the liver, spleen, and legs.
questions.suggestedLabel: D. a heart murmur.
questions.suggestedRationale: Aortic stenosis produces a characteristic systolic murmur; cardiac output tends to fall, not rise.

questions.prompt: Effects that may be expected from a beta-adrenergic blocking drug include
options: decreased sympathetic stimulation of the heart.
blockage of an angiotensin receptor site.
questions.suggestedLabel: B. decreased sympathetic stimulation of the heart.
questions.suggestedRationale: Beta blockers decrease sympathetic stimulation of the heart (and can reduce renin release).

questions.prompt: In an infant, the initial indication of congestive heart failure is often
questions.suggestedLabel: B. feeding problems.
questions.suggestedRationale: In infants, feeding difficulty (and poor weight gain or sweating with feeds) is often the first clue to heart failure.

questions.prompt: Which of the following drugs improves cardiac efficiency by slowing the heart rate and increasing the force of cardiac contractions?
questions.suggestedLabel: B. Digoxin
questions.suggestedRationale: Digoxin slows conduction/heart rate and increases the force of contraction.

questions.prompt: In which blood vessels will failure of the left ventricle cause increased hydrostatic pressure?
options: Veins of the legs and feet
Blood vessels of the liver and spleen
questions.suggestedLabel: C. Pulmonary capillaries
questions.suggestedRationale: Left-ventricular failure raises hydrostatic pressure in the pulmonary capillaries, causing pulmonary congestion or edema.

questions.prompt: Compensation mechanisms for decreased cardiac output in cases of congestive heart failure include
questions.suggestedLabel: B. increased renin and aldosterone secretions.
questions.suggestedRationale: Decreased cardiac output activates renin–angiotensin–aldosterone, which retains salt and water and is a major CHF compensation.

questions.prompt: Significant signs of right-sided congestive heart failure include
options: edematous feet and legs with hepatomegaly.
frequent cough with blood-streaked frothy sputum.
questions.suggestedLabel: B. edematous feet and legs with hepatomegaly.
questions.suggestedRationale: Right-sided failure causes systemic backup: leg edema and hepatomegaly. Frothy blood-streaked sputum is a left-sided (pulmonary edema) sign.
